# the contributor audit of the new paired and forest invariants

These are independent bounded audits. None certifies the full OC goal.

## Reflected discrepancy and the two-layer median region: PASS

Read `candidate e18e6db2f3e079d5` in full and independently derived its cap reflection identity. Complementary ordinary halfspaces exchange signed discrepancies v and (b-a)-v. This proves that their positive supremum is the absolute discrepancy; the unequal total masses are tracked correctly. Vertical caps cannot lower the formula because the discrepancy is at least b-a.

The translation Lipschitz bound follows from a uniform section-area bound, and the compact actual Minkowski section contains all positive-depth points. Its boundary has zero endpoint depth, so a positive maximum is attained in its interior. Full-budget depth a is equivalent to reflected containment of the smaller body: otherwise strict separation of a missing point produces a positive-volume cap in the smaller full-dimensional body. The support-gap homothetic cap has the stated volume and sign. The same-normal expression after adding the middle body retains the common normal before taking a lower bound by separate minima at ONE fixed point.

The 225-case exact verifier passes. No volume-only optimized discrepancy estimate is supplied or assumed.

## Two-layer and simplex-source inverse quantiles: PASS

Read all seven sections of `candidate 0fcbc670d417c3ed`. The inverse of a strictly decreasing concave cap-root profile is decreasing and concave; the direction of its inversion is correct. A zero-volume support face remains nonempty, so ordinary cap Brunn--Minkowski covers the support endpoint.

The allocation sphere is compact, fixed independently of R, and every coordinate stays in its quantile domain because R is below every source volume root. An infimum of concave functions is concave. Strict decrease follows either by the compact positive-difference argument in the note or by evaluating the later objective at a minimizer of the earlier one.

The strict sublevel equivalence is exact. If the threshold sum exceeds a minimizing quantile sum, raising all thresholds gives a strictly smaller positive cap budget. Conversely, a total below R^d can be enlarged to exactly R^d in the source volumes, lowering at least one quantile threshold strictly. Empty caps use the supporting threshold inequality; R strictly below all full source volumes removes saturation in this step. The full-mass plateau follows by taking all strict R below its endpoint, not by treating an empty set as a nonempty cap in BM.

The decreasing inverse is concave on the required support interval, including its left constant plateau. It is not extended as a concave function past the right zero boundary. All candidates in the actual Minkowski section obey every directional support bound. Taking the infimum over normals is therefore legitimate. Vertical source caps contain a full source and cannot lower the formula. Affinely independent bases yield precisely one weighted threshold constraint; singleton sources are explicitly qualified. The same-point addition of a middle source is valid, but its separate positive-root terms cannot be combined into a new concavity assertion.

The 1,638 exact-profile checks and the separate dependent-source values pass. The old interval counter lies partly outside the endpoint Minkowski section; the new planar certificate below independently closes that possible loophole.

## Actual roof patches and the eight-node exchange: PASS

Read `candidate 39e0ea36e1546d5b` in full. Actual radius concavity and finite linear-programming duality give an affine upper majorant at each sampled graph point, including boundary bases. A midpoint in a minimal face puts both endpoints in that face. Terminal paths therefore enlarge minimal faces in the asserted direction.

Every integer point of a projected root patch receives a positive Minkowski fiber. Its radius simultaneously lies above the interpolated affine roof and below its supporting majorant, so equality holds and the point belongs to the same face. Equal-radius anchored inclusions of the common shape give equal actual centroids. A strictly positive representation of the relative-interior root lets one perturb every affine dependence in both signs, proving affine centroid coordinates on the entire patch.

The exact two-patch mass counterexample retains the overlap once. Its claimed conclusion is only the failure of independent patch budgeting. The successful eight-node argument instead has five disjoint weight blocks A,G,L,B,C. The two distinct directions at candidate4 supply B+min(G,C), where the grouped C nodes share a ray. For C<=G, the four blocks A,G,L,B+C are each bounded by D; for C>G, the four blocks A,L,B+G,C are each bounded by D because C<=B+G. Thus T<=4D. No mass is counted twice inside either case. Exact verifier PASS.

## Actual nine-base graph obstruction and continuous compensation: PASS

Read `candidate 90f577d65c14ec9f` in full and ran its exact verifier PASS. The triangle support enumeration, positive concave roof, canonical root ties, and all exact set-equivalent midpoint equations check. Every displayed graph halfspace includes its boundary atoms. The table gives an upper bound2V at every graph candidate, while the equal opposite pair at root1 gives the matching lower bound2V.

The all-dimensional parameter R=63d-7 satisfies the claimed strict binomial inequality, so the fixed exact graph incidence fails the quarter-mass graph bound for every d. This is a graph assertion only. The actual equal three-fiber block at root1 contributes an own Gamma_d V term and a paired 2 Gamma_d V term. A vertical cap contributes at least2V, which is sufficient because Gamma_d<=1/2. Since the full mass is at most9V, the actual point has depth at least Gamma_d/3. Central symmetry is used only for the separate interval illustration. This source is explicitly not an OC counterexample.

## Dependent root concavity fails inside the actual Minkowski section: PASS

Read `candidate 4c55389e587862a0` in full and ran its exact verifier PASS. The three fibers T, (-1/8,-1/8)+(7/4)T, 2T form the stated exact actual sections. No fiber has half of total mass, and the middle and larger endpoint are incomparable.

At y=(t,t), 0<t<=1/3, the two endpoints contain the same triangle3tT with centroid y, and the middle contains (-1/8,-1/8)+3(t+1/8)T with that same centroid. Paired tails and ordinary triangle Grünbaum therefore give the lower bound4t^2+2(t+1/8)^2 for ALL ambient caps. The single cap x1+x2<=2t attains it exactly. All three rational test points lie strictly inside (3/2)T. The radical comparison441<473 and the positive second-derivative numerator32delta^2 are correct.

The separate point(1/2,1/2) pays at least1: half a unit from the contained middle triangle and half a unit from the reflected endpoint containment. The OC target is43/48. Thus the example only refutes the proposed concavity strengthening, without contradicting OC.
